mainTopic: Conditions in a גט: returning the paper, a dying man's wording, and serving the father or nursing the son
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a ברייתא where a man gives a גט on condition that the paper be returned to him. רב אדא בר אהבה says the condition is void because the condition and the action are about the same thing. רב אשי instead says the ברייתא follows רבי, for whom 'על מנת' works like 'מעכשיו', so the divorce takes effect right away. Next, שמואל sets a wording for the גט of a dying man. The גמרא explains why the negative side comes first, and רבא then replaces it with a three-part wording that puts 'yes' before 'no', as in the condition of בני גד ובני ראובן. A new משנה follows about a גט given on condition that the wife serve the husband's father or nurse his son. The time allowed, and what happens if the son or father dies, depend on whether a time was stated, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees. The גמרא contrasts this משנה with a ברייתא that says one day is enough, and רב חסדא, רבא and רב אשי each answer differently. The amud ends with a new objection to רב אשי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Condition and action are about the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge against the earlier explanation: the condition should be void for a simpler reason, because the condition and the action concern the same matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Why give that reason? You could simply say the condition fails] because the condition and the action are about one and the same matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against the explanation given just before this. It says there is a simpler reason the condition does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanation gave one reason why the condition to return the paper does not hold. The challenge says that reason is not even needed. The condition and the action are both about the same thing, the גט itself, and such a condition is void anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition attached to an act
The action itself, here the giving of the גט
About one and the same matter

phrases.english: since the condition and the action are about one matter!
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question that starts on the previous lines. The condition (return the paper) and the action (giving the גט) both involve the same paper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a challenge against the explanation given before this text begins
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation for why the condition in the ברייתא is not effective
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That explanation is unnecessary, because a condition that is about the same matter as the action is void anyway.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה gives the real reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה accepts the challenge: the condition is void because condition and action are about the same matter, so the גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא בר אהבה said: it is because the condition and the action are about one matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier explanation and adopts the reason from the challenge, in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the old reason is set aside. The condition is void because it is about the same thing as the action. So the woman is divorced even if the condition is not kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier view and gives a new one
An אמורא who gives the accepted reason here

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It is because the condition and the action are about one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge and makes its point the official reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reason with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא needed the earlier, more complicated reason
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition is void because it concerns the same matter as the action, so the גט is valid
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אדא בר אהבה, a condition that is about the very same thing as the action is void, and the act stands.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the ברייתא another way: it follows רבי, who holds that 'על מנת' means 'from now', so the divorce takes effect right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Whose view is this? It is רבי's. As רב הונא said in the name of רב: anyone who says 'on condition' is like one who says 'from now'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different way to explain the ברייתא. He says it follows the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, saying 'על מנת' is the same as saying 'מעכשיו', from now. So the גט works right away, and the condition, giving back the paper, only has to be kept later. That is why the woman is divorced at once, without needing רב אדא בר אהבה's reason that the condition is void.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Asks which תנא a source follows
On condition that
From now; takes effect right away
Is like; is treated the same as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'על מנת' delays the divorce until the condition is kept. In רבי's view the divorce happens now, and the condition is only kept afterward.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi's,
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same ברייתא instead of רב אדא בר אהבה's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to need the reason that the condition is void
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי, so 'על מנת' works as 'מעכשיו' and the גט takes effect immediately
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'כל האומר על מנת כאומר מעכשיו דמי' is a major principle about conditions that comes up in many places in ש״ס.

steps.title: שמואל's wording for a dying man's גט
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: שמואל set a fixed wording for the גט of a שכיב מרע, saying first 'if I do not die, it is not a גט' and then 'if I die, it is a גט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל set a rule for the גט of a dying man: 'If I do not die, it will not be a גט; and if I die, it will be a גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It reports a wording that שמואל set for a גט given by a man who is very sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sick man wants the גט to work only if he dies, so his wife will not need יבום or חליצה. The wording states both sides of the condition, what happens if he dies and what happens if he lives. The negative side comes first, and the next step asks why.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up; made a rule (a תקנה)
A person who is very sick and may die
If I do not die
It will be a valid גט

phrases.english: Shmuel set a rule for the bill of divorce of a dying man:
'If I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce,
and if I die, it will be a bill of divorce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about conditions in a גט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dying man's גט should say: 'If I do not die it is not a גט, and if I die it is a גט.'

steps.title: Why not put the positive side first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל did not use the more natural order: 'if I die it is a גט' first, and 'if I do not die it is not' second.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say: 'If I die it will be a גט, and if I do not die it will not be a גט'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the order of שמואל's wording. It suggests a more natural order and is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the main case, what makes the גט work, would be said first. שמואל put the negative side first. The גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say; suggests a different wording

phrases.english: But let him say: 'If I die, it will be a bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא מַתִּי לֹא יְהֵא גֵּט״!
phrases.english: and if I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the order of the wording שמואל set
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the two halves in שמואל's wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The natural order puts the case that makes the גט work first, so why reverse it?

steps.title: A person does not mention his own misfortune first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a person does not want to bring up his own death first, so the wording starts with 'if I do not die'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person does not bring up a misfortune for himself first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the order of שמואל's wording. A sick man does not want to start by talking about his own death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is not about the law but about how people feel. Opening with 'if I die' would be like inviting bad luck. So the wording opens with the hopeful side, 'if I do not die'.

keyTerms.meaning: Puts first; brings early
Misfortune; calamity
For himself

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's deathbed גט says the hopeful side first ('if I do not die') because a person does not mention his own death first.

phrases.english: A person does not bring up a misfortune for himself first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about word order
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording by how people naturally speak and feel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The positive side should come first, since it is the main case
steps.terutzMaskana: The negative side comes first so the sick man does not mention his own death first

steps.title: Why not put the result before the condition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל did not say 'it will not be a גט if I do not die,' putting the result first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say: 'It will not be a גט if I do not die!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests another way to word the first clause. It flips the order so the result ('not a גט') comes before the condition ('if I do not die').
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 explained that the man opens with 'if I do not die' so he does not mention his death first. The גמרא now asks why he does not open with 'it will not be a גט' instead. That wording would also avoid mentioning death first, so why did שמואל choose his particular order?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say. This proposes a different wording.
A person who is dangerously ill.

phrases.english: But let him say: 'It will not be a bill of divorce
if I do not die'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 6 and suggests another wording that would also avoid mentioning death first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the words in שמואל's first clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only goal is to avoid opening with death, putting the result first would also work. So why did שמואל choose his order?

steps.title: The condition must come before the action
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in a valid תנאי, the condition has to be stated before the action it controls.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need the condition to come before the action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the suggested wording is not allowed. A condition must be stated before the result it controls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule for conditions: first say the 'if,' then say the result. 'Not a גט if I do not die' puts the result first, so it breaks this rule. That is why שמואל said 'if I do not die' first.

keyTerms.meaning: The condition must come before the action.
We need it to be so.

phrases.english: We require the condition to come before the action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a legal rule that the suggested wording breaks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any order of the words works, as long as death is not mentioned first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'if' has to come before the result, so שמואל's order is needed.

steps.title: רבא: positive must come before negative
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to שמואל's wording. All conditions are learned from בני גד ובני ראובן, where the 'yes' side comes first, but שמואל starts with the 'no' side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: Where do we learn all the rules of conditions from? From the condition of בני גד and בני ראובן. Just as there the 'yes' comes before the 'no,' so too in all conditions the 'yes' must come before the 'no.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges שמואל's whole wording. He points out that שמואל puts the negative side ('if I do not die, not a גט') before the positive side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of תנאים come from משה's deal with בני גד ובני ראובן. There, the positive side ('if they cross, give them the land') is said before the negative side. שמואל's wording starts with the negative, so it fails a basic rule of conditions.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, a strong challenge.
משה's condition with the tribes of גד and ראובן, the source for all conditions.
The 'yes' side comes before the 'no' side.
Now, after all. It opens a basic point.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. 'Condition before action' (step 8) is about the 'if' coming before the result. 'Yes before no' is about the positive case coming before the negative case. רבא's point is the second rule.

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
Now, all conditions,
from where do we learn them?
From the condition of the children of Gad and the children of Reuben;
just as there, the 'yes' comes before the 'no,'
so too all conditions: the 'yes' must come before the 'no.'
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets fill in the end of the sentence. Some versions don't have them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after step 8 defended שמואל's order, רבא raises a different rule that שמואל's wording breaks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All conditions follow the model of בני גד ובני ראובן, where the 'yes' comes before the 'no.' שמואל starts with the 'no,' so his wording is not a proper תנאי.

steps.title: רבא's three-part wording
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new wording: 'if I do not die it is not a גט; if I die it is a גט; if I do not die it is not a גט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'If I do not die, it will not be a גט. If I die, it will be a גט. If I do not die, it will not be a גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces שמואל's wording with a new one. It has three clauses, and the 'not a גט' line appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps שמואל's opening line. After it, he adds a full condition in the correct order: 'yes' first, then 'no.' The next step explains why each part is there.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, he said. It brings a new approach instead of the one just rejected.
If I die.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'If I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce;
if I die, it will be a bill of divorce;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא מַתִּי לֹא יְהֵא גֵּט״ –
phrases.english: if I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting שמואל's wording in step 9, רבא offers his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שכיב מרע's גט should say: 'If I do not die it is not a גט; if I die it is a גט; if I do not die it is not a גט.'

steps.title: Why each part of רבא's wording is needed
steps.stepSummary: The first line keeps him from opening with his own death. The next two lines make a proper condition with 'yes' before 'no.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If I do not die, it will not be a גט' comes first, because a person does not bring up trouble for himself first. Then 'if I die it will be a גט, if I do not die it will not be a גט,' because the 'yes' must come before the 'no.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's wording has three parts. Each part solves a different problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line respects the man's feelings: he does not start by talking about his death. The last two lines are the real legal condition, in the order learned from בני גד ובני ראובן. So both concerns are met at once.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not bring up trouble for himself first.
Trouble, a disaster. Here it means his death.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's wording handles two things. The opening 'if I do not die, not a גט' avoids starting with death. Then 'if I die, a גט; if I do not die, not a גט' is a proper condition with the 'yes' before the 'no,' just like בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exact wording of a תנאי matters. It has to follow the model of בני גד ובני ראובן, while still being sensitive to how a sick person feels.

phrases.english: 'If I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce' comes first because
a person does not bring first
trouble upon himself;
'If I die, it will be a bill of divorce;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא מַתִּי לֹא יְהֵא גֵּט״ –
phrases.english: if I do not die, it will not be a bill of divorce' comes next because
we require the 'yes' to come before the 'no.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording רבא gave in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opening line respects the man's feelings, and the next two lines are a proper condition with 'yes' before 'no.'

steps.title: New משנה: a גט on condition to serve the father or nurse the son, with no time stated
steps.stepSummary: A husband gives a גט on condition that his wife serve his father or nurse his son, without saying for how long. She must nurse for two years, while רבי יהודה says eighteen months. If the son or the father dies, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man says, 'This is your גט on condition that you serve my father,' or 'on condition that you nurse my son,' how long must she nurse him? Two years. רבי יהודה says eighteen months. If the son died or the father died, the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a גט that depends on a תנאי of serving the husband's father or nursing his son, when no amount of time was mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the husband named no time, the משנה fills in the normal length of nursing: two years, or eighteen months according to רבי יהודה. If the son or father dies, she cannot finish the job, yet the גט still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
On condition that. This is the standard phrase for making a תנאי.
That you serve, meaning to take care of someone.
That you nurse, meaning to breastfeed.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you serve my father";
or "on condition that you nurse my son" –
how long does she nurse him?
Two years.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Eighteen months.
If the son died or the father died –
phrases.notes: 'The father' here is the husband's father, the one she was supposed to serve.

phrases.english: it is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of שמואל's wording of a תנאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no time is stated, nursing means two years (רבי יהודה says eighteen months). If the son or father dies, the גט is valid.

steps.title: When two years are stated outright and the son dies or the father refuses, it is not a גט
steps.stepSummary: If the husband names two years and the son dies, or the father says he does not want her service, the גט is not valid. This holds even if the father was not angry with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'This is your גט on condition that you serve my father for two years,' or 'nurse my son for two years,' and the son died, or the father said 'I don't want you to serve me' without being angry, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now changes the case: this time the husband clearly said 'two years.' If she could not complete the two years, the תנא קמא says the גט does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the time was spelled out as part of the תנאי, so it must actually be fulfilled. Even when the failure is not her fault, the condition was still not met. That is why the גט fails, even if the father refused without any anger toward her.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not want.
Being upset or angry, taking offense.
It is not a valid גט.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. When no time was stated (step 12), the death of the son or father leaves the גט valid. When 'two years' was stated outright (this step), the תנא קמא says it is not a גט.

phrases.english: "This is your bill of divorce on condition
that you serve my father for two years";

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּנִיקִי אֶת בְּנִי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״ –
phrases.english: or "on condition that you nurse my son for two years" –
and the son died,
or the father said:
"I do not want you to serve me"
not out of anger –
it is not a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 12: the same condition, but now with the time stated outright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the time was stated outright and the condition cannot be completed, even through no fault of hers, it is not a גט.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a hindrance that is not from her leaves the גט valid
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and says the גט is valid in this case. He gives a general rule: whenever the hindrance does not come from her, it is a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: in a case like this, it is a גט. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל stated a general rule: any hindrance that does not come from her, it is a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues with the previous ruling. He holds the גט is valid when the son dies or the father refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, what matters is whose fault the failure is. If she was ready to do her part and something outside her control stopped her, the condition counts as fulfilled. He turns this into a broad rule for all such cases.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this.
A general rule.
A hindrance, something that holds back the fulfillment.
From her, meaning caused by her.

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says a condition with a stated time must actually be fulfilled, so if she cannot complete it, it is not a גט. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the hindrance is not from her, it is a גט.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
in a case like this, it is a bill of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a general rule:
any hindrance that does not come from her –
it is a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: כָּזֶה גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any hindrance to fulfilling the condition that does not come from her leaves the גט valid.

steps.title: Does she really need to serve or nurse that long? A ברייתא says one day is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's demand of two years. A ברייתא teaches that if she served or nursed for even one day, the גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Do we really need all this? A contradiction was raised from a ברייתא: if she served him one day, or nursed him one day, it is a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the משנה. Why require two full years, when a ברייתא says one day is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies the full time must be completed. The ברייתא says one day of serving or nursing makes the גט valid. These two sources seem to clash, and the גמרא will need to resolve the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה. Written here as the short form גְּמָ׳.
All this much.
And they raised a contradiction. This is the formula for bringing a source that clashes with the one being studied.
One day.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But do we require all this?!
phrases.notes: 'All this' means the full two years the משנה speaks about.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
if she served him for one day,
or she nursed him for one day –
it is a bill of divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's requirement of a full time period.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that she must serve or nurse for the full two years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that one day of serving or nursing makes the גט valid, which contradicts requiring the whole period.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the two sources follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers the contradiction by assigning the משנה to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the ברייתא to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is not a contradiction. One source follows the רבנן, and the other follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from step 15. He says the משנה and the ברייתא simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not try to make the two sources agree. He says that each one reflects a different תנא. In his view, the משנה, which demands the full two years, follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who looks at the real benefit the husband wanted. The ברייתא, which accepts even one day, follows the רבנן, who read the condition by its literal words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard opening of an answer.
This one... and that one. Used to split two sources between two cases or two opinions.
Our משנה
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: it is not difficult:
this one is the Rabbis,
and this one is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
The Mishnah follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and the baraita follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: each source follows a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to give opposite rulings on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not need to agree. The משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The first clause cannot be רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב חסדא: since the later clause of the משנה is credited to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first clause must belong to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part of the משנה is said in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that shows the first part is not his opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. The way the משנה is built shows that the first part cannot be the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ends with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagreeing (step 14). If he disagrees in the סיפא, the רישא, which requires two years, must be the opinion of the רבנן. So רב חסדא cannot assign the משנה's two-year ruling to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
By implication, meaning 'which shows that'

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the part where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the גט is valid (step 14).

phrases.english: is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
it follows that the first clause
is not Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's assignment in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the סיפא is credited to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as a dissent, the רישא must belong to the רבנן.

steps.title: Flip it: the ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the assignment. The ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is lenient with conditions, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is lenient about conditions. The משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב חסדא's answer by switching which opinion goes with which source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the משנה itself. In step 14, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who is easygoing about conditions. So he is the one who would accept even one day of nursing, as the ברייתא says. The רבנן demand more, which is why they require the full two years in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals a corrected version of the answer.
Is lenient
Conditions

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רב חסדא: the משנה (two years) follows the רבנן, and the ברייתא (one day) follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is lenient with conditions.

phrases.english: Rather, the baraita
is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who is lenient with conditions;
the Mishnah is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בָּרַיְיתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects רב חסדא's answer after the challenge in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing which opinion goes with which source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is lenient with conditions, and the משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא: unspecified time versus a clearly stated time
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: the משנה is about a husband who named no time, and the ברייתא is about a husband who clearly stated one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not a contradiction. Here, the husband spoke without naming a time. There, he spelled it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer to the contradiction. He says the two sources are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבא's answer, there is no need to say the sources disagree. When the husband says nothing about time (the משנה), she must nurse for the normal length, which is two years. When he clearly says one day (the ברייתא), one day is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Without specifying; nothing was spelled out
Specifies; spells it out clearly
Here... there. Used to split two sources between two different cases.

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the contradiction: רב חסדא says it is a מחלוקת (the משנה follows the רבנן and the ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). רבא says these are two different cases (the husband named no time, or he clearly named a time).

phrases.english: Rava said: it is not difficult:
here, where it was unspecified,
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is our משנה, where the husband named no time. The second is the ברייתא, where he clearly said one day.

phrases.english: there, where it was specified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּסְתָם, כָּאן בִּמְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the step 15 contradiction instead of רב חסדא's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources describe the same case and give opposite rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a case where no time was stated, so the normal two years applies. The ברייתא is a case where one day was explicitly stated.

steps.title: רב אשי: An Open-Ended Condition Means One Day
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that when no time was named, the condition is treated as if the husband explicitly said 'one day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Any condition stated without a time is also treated like one where he clearly said 'one day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer from רבא to the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that an open-ended condition requires the full normal amount of time. רב אשי disagrees: if the husband named no time, one day is enough. So the ברייתא's 'one day' applies even when the husband was silent about time.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain, unspecified, with no details given
One who states explicitly
Is considered like, is equal to
Also, too

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Any unspecified condition too
is like one who explicitly said "one day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction, different from רבא's answer in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the default meaning of an unspecified condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unspecified condition requires the full standard period, so it contradicts the ברייתא's one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unspecified condition is like saying 'one day,' so the ברייתא's one day applies to it.

steps.title: The משנה's Two Years Seem to Contradict רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets nursing at two years (or eighteen months). That fits רבא, but according to רב אשי one day should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: How long does she nurse him? Two years. רבי יהודה says: eighteen months. This works well for רבא. But according to רב אשי, why do we need two years? Why do we need eighteen months? One day should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי from the משנה, which gives a full nursing period of two years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא can explain the משנה easily, since an open-ended condition needs the normal nursing time. For רב אשי, open-ended means one day, so the משנה should not need to mention two years or eighteen months at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Granted, this works for one opinion
It fits well
Why do I need it?
It is enough

phrases.english: We learned: How long is she to nurse him?
Two years.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: eighteen months.
Granted, according to Rava, it works well;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, לְמָה לִי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים?
phrases.english: but according to Rav Ashi, why do I need two years?
Why do I need eighteen months?
One day is enough!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא נִיחָא אֶלָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer from Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that an unspecified condition equals one day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names a long period for an open-ended nursing condition, which makes no sense if one day is enough.

steps.title: The Two Years Mark the Window for the One Day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that the one day must fall within the first two years (or eighteen months) of the baby's life, not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: one day within the two years, which excludes nursing after two years, which does not count. One day within the eighteen months, which excludes nursing after eighteen months, which does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי by reading the משנה's numbers in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two years (or eighteen months) are not how long she must nurse. They are the nursing age, the period during which her one day of nursing must take place. Nursing a child older than that does not fulfill the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
To exclude
That it does not count

steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, 'two years' no longer means how long she must nurse. It now means the time window, the baby's first two years, in which the one day must fall.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
one day within the two years;
to exclude after two years, which does not count.
One day within the eighteen months;
phrases.notes: This is the same answer, worked out for רבי יהודה's opinion.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי לְאַחַר שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ – דְּלָא.
phrases.english: to exclude after eighteen months, which does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 and keeps רב אשי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's two years means she must nurse for the full two years.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two years is the window in which one day of nursing must happen. Nursing after that window does not count.

steps.title: New Objection: The Son Died or the Father Refused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ruling that if the son died, or the father declined her service even without anger, the גט is not valid. This sets up a new challenge to רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'This is your גט on condition that you serve my father for two years,' or 'on condition that you nurse my son for two years.' If the son died, or the father said 'I do not want you to serve me,' even not in anger, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new objection to רב אשי by quoting this ruling. The full argument from it continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is strict: if she cannot complete the condition because the son died or the father refused her, the גט fails, even though the father was not angry with her. The גמרא will use this strict ruling to test רב אשי's lenient view that one day can be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from an earlier teaching)
On condition that
I do not want
Anger or being upset

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתְּשַׁמְּשִׁי אֶת אַבָּא שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״;
phrases.english: on condition that you serve my father for two years";

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּנִיקִי אֶת בְּנִי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים״ –
phrases.english: "on condition that you nurse my son for two years"
if the son died,
or the father said, "I do not want you to serve me"
not in anger, it is not a valid bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב אשי in Step 22, the גמרא raises a new objection to him from a teaching whose wording matches the second case of our משנה (step 13).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that one day can fulfill the condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling invalidates the גט when the son dies or the father refuses her service. This strictness seems hard to fit with the idea that one day is enough. The precise argument comes in the next lines.
